verdict.rationale: Parahelp documents tools that call any API, including Stripe or your own internal endpoints, and shows a refund tool. Each tool can be individually gated behind Slack human approval or set to auto-approve per task, which gives per-action control. However, the evidence shows no per-action credential or permission scoping; connections are set up once and shared by both agents. Missing for 10: documented scoped auth/credentials per action, explicit order-change and subscription-update examples, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the agent takes real actions through my APIs — refunds, order changes, subscription updates — with scoped auth per action

citations.quote: Tools can use any service with an API: public integrations like Stripe, or your own internal endpoints.
Require Slack approval before the refund tool runs on amounts above $100.
Any tool can be gated behind human approval. Gated actions are sent to Slack with approve and deny buttons, and nothing runs until someone on your team approves.
By default, every action requires manual approval. You can set specific tools to auto-approve per task or automation
